adjudication.rationale: Verified in the diff. In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` `updateEvent`, the fallback assigns `selectedCalendar` as `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;`. When `externalCalendarId` is falsy (e.g., `null`/`undefined`), the `find` compares `cal.externalId` to that same falsy value, so it will almost always return `undefined`. The same pattern exists in `deleteEvent` (`calendarId = externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;`). Since callers in this diff can pass a falsy externalCalendarId (e.g., `EventManager.updateCalendarEvent` sets `calenderExternalId` to `null` if absent), these paths will target `primary` (delete) or use an undefined calendar id / fallback, risking updates/deletes on the wrong calendar and leaving non-primary events orphaned.
